Methods of Chemical Analysis of Ferrous Metals Sectional Committee^ SMDC 2 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( Part 3 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 17 October 
1988, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Chemical Analysis of Ferrous Metals Sectional 
Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council. 

The chemical analysis of diflFerent ferro-alloys, namely, ferrosilicon, ferrochromium, ferromanganese 
and speigeleisen, silicomanganese, ferro-molybdenum, ferrophosphorus, ferrotitanium, fcrro- 
vanadium and ferrotungsten have been covered in IS 1559: 1961 'Methods of chemical analysis of 
ferro-alloys'. While reviewing this standard, the sectional committee had decided that separate 
series of standards for each of the ferro-alloys should be prepared. Accordingly, the chemical 
analysis of ferrosilicon were covered in various parts of IS : 1559. 

The chemical analysis of ferro-molybdenum is now covered in several parts of this standard ( IS 12614 ). 
With the publication of these parts, the analysis of relevant constituents prescribed for ferro-molyb- 
denum in IS 1559: 1961 will be superseded. This part covers the method for determination of 
silicon. The other parts are : 

Part 1 Determination of molybdenum 
Part 2 Determination of total carbon 
Part 4 Determination of sulphur 
Part 5 Determination of phosphorus 
Part 6 Determination of copper 
Part 7 Determination of aluminium 

In this revision, the gravimetric method for determination of silicon has been retained and updated. 

In reporting the result of a test of analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, 
observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : I960 *Rules 
for rounding oflF numerical values ( revised )\ 



IS 12614 ( Part 3 ) : 1988 



Indian Standard 



METHODS OF CHEMICAL 
ANALYSIS OF FERRO-MOLYBDENUM 

PART 3 DETERMINATION OF SILICON 



1 SCOPE 

This standard ( Part 3 ) covers the gravimetric 
method for determination of silicon in ferro- 
molybdenum. 

2 REFERENCES 

The Indian Standard IS 1472: 1977 'Methods 
of sampling ferro-alloys for determination of 
chemical composition {first revision )' is a neces- 
sary adjunct to this standard. 

3 SAMPLING 

Sample shall be drawn and prepared in accord- 
ance with IS 1472: 1977. 

4 Q,UALITY OF REAGENTS 

Unless specified otherwise, analystical grade 
reagents and distilled water shall be employed in 
the tests. 

5 DETERMINATION OF SILICON BY 
GRAVIMETRIC METHOD 

5.1 Outline of the Method 

The sample is decomposed with nitric acid and 
sulphuric acid followed by dehydration, filtration 
of silica, hydrofluorization and computing the 
silica. 

5.2 Reagents 

5.2.1 Dilute Nitric Acid, 1 : 3 ( v/v ). 

5.2.2 Dilute Sulphuric Acid, 1 : 1 ( v/v ). 

5.2.3 Dilute Hydrochloric Acid, 1 : 4 ( v/v ) and 

1 : 20 ( v/v ). 



5.2.4 Hydrofluoric Acid, 40 per cent. 

5.3 Procedure 

5-3,l Transfer 1 g of the accurately weighed 
sample to a 400-ml pyrex glass beaker and add 
25 ml of dilute nitric acid. When the reaction 
ceases, add 15 ml of dilute sulphuric acid and 
evaporate to dense white fuir.es of sulphur 
trioxide. Cool, add 75 ml dilute hydrochloric 
acid (1:4), heat till all soluble salts have 
dissolved, and filter immediately. Wash the filter 
and the residue with hot dilute hydrochloric acid 
( 1 : 20 ) and with hot water alternately and 
finally with hot water till free from chlorides 
and sulphates. 

5.3.2 Place the paper and residue in the platinum 
crucible and dry completely on a hot plate. Heat 
the crucible at 1 OOO^'C to a constant mass. 

5.3.3 Add suflBcient dilute sulphuric acid to 
moisten the residue, then add carefully about 3 
to 5 ml of hydrofluoric acid and cautiously 
evaporate to dryness and ignite to constant mass. 

5.4 Blank 

A blank determination shall be carried out with 
all the reagents used above. 



(A-B) X 46-74 



5.5 Calculation 

Silicon, percent == 

where 
A = mass of silica obtained from the 
sample, in g 

S = mass of silica obtained in the blank, in 

g, and 
C = mass of the sample taken, in g. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards.
